rsr_notes.note: «Aurore» is Bouguereau's painting (Marie says «une Aurore de Bouguereau» in 103.0058) and «Phèdre» is Cabanel's; the LAN note giving both to Cabanel is wrong.
«Aurore» is Bouguereau's painting, not Cabanel's, and «Phèdre» is Cabanel's; the LAN note crediting both to Cabanel should be corrected.
«Les Horaces, le Serment de Grutli» most likely means David's painting Le Serment des Horaces (the oath, with the Grutli oath as a pendant joke), not Corneille's Horace.
The Stabat Mater sung is not identified by composer (Rossini's is probable but unproved); no work tag.
The Stabat Mater is not attributed to a composer by Marie; Rossini's is probable (chorus) but unproved, so no tag.
Marie's reading list also names Bulwer's The Last Days of Pompeii, which has no glossary entry yet.
«Mabel Waughan» is Maria Cummins's Mabel Vaughan (1857); The Lamplighter is only named as its author's earlier book.
Hamlet read in English is Shakespeare's play; the music is Ambroise Thomas's opera Hamlet.
Ira Aldridge is footnoted as Othello; Marie does not name the play or any performance here.
Hamlet read here in English is Shakespeare's play; the Ambroise Thomas opera is the music she hums.
Rienzi here is Cola di Rienzo the tribune (as in Bulwer-Lytton's novel), not Wagner's opera.
«Les Femmes de la Bible» is a separate book she buys, not the Bible itself.
«Le drapeau» is another painting by Georges Bertrand, not Printemps qui passe.
«l'étincelle» here means the spark of genius, not Pailleron's play.
«Rienzi» here is Wagner's opera at the Teatro Pagliano, not Bulwer-Lytton's novel.
The English book quoted here is not identified and may not be the Nice novel (Mrs Bodgers) of 051.0222.
Nausicaa is the Odyssey princess; Marie does not name the epic here.
